message: Generated a 7-section Project Plan "Customer Support Migration from Zendesk to Freshdesk" (~1695 words) for Customer Support leadership, IT project sponsors, and implementation team. It made 5 documented assumption(s). Self-review score 8/10 → 7/10 → 9/10 after revising 6 section(s).

document.title: Customer Support Migration from Zendesk to Freshdesk

analysis.title: Customer Support Migration from Zendesk to Freshdesk
analysis.subtitle: 8‑week migration plan for 25 agents
analysis.audience: Customer Support leadership, IT project sponsors, and implementation team
analysis.objective: Provide a clear roadmap, budget, risks and success metrics to ensure a smooth migration within 8 weeks
missing_information: Exact licensing cost per seat for Freshdesk
Detailed risk register (specific technical or compliance risks)
Target thresholds for each success metric
Names of internal stakeholders beyond assumed leads
assumptions: Project starts on 30 Oct 2026 (Friday) and runs for exactly 8 weeks, ending 24 Dec 2026 (Thursday)
Budget breakdown: $50,000 licensing, $30,000 consulting services, $20,000 data migration, $20,000 training & change management
Project lead is Priya Sharma, Migration lead is Alex Johnson, Support manager is Maya Patel, IT Operations lead is Carlos Ruiz
Success metrics thresholds: ≥95% tickets migrated without data loss, average handling time within 5% of baseline, agent satisfaction ≥8/10, 100% support coverage first week post‑go‑live
key_facts: Training & change management budget: $20,000 (16.7% of total)

plan_rationale: The structure follows a standard project plan flow, starting with scope and moving through execution details (timeline, roles, budget) to risk management and success criteria, ensuring all explicit requirements are addressed for the leadership audience.

todo.title: Understand request: type, audience, gaps, conflicts
Self-review against the request; revise weak sections

issues.problem: Risk R03 proposes adding a 1‑week buffer to Phase 2 and a $5,000 contingency budget, which conflicts with the fixed 8‑week schedule and the total budget of $120,000 defined in the fact sheet.
issues.fix: Remove the suggestion of a 1‑week buffer and the $5,000 contingency from the mitigation strategy, or adjust the overall timeline and budget to accommodate them while keeping the project within the 8‑week, $120,000 constraints.

issues.problem: The success metrics section schedules a post‑go‑live agent satisfaction survey on 26 Dec 2026, which is after the project end date of 24 Dec 2026.
issues.fix: Move the survey date to 24 Dec 2026 (the last day of the project) or incorporate it into the hyper‑care period, ensuring all success metrics are measured by the project end date.

issues.problem: Risk R08 allocates an extra $3,000 for additional connectors, which is not reflected in the $120,000 total budget breakdown, creating a budget inconsistency.
issues.fix: Remove the $3,000 allocation or re‑classify it within one of the existing budget categories so that the summed total remains $120,000.

issues.problem: The success metrics state that first‑week support coverage will be verified from 24 Dec 2026 to 31 Dec 2026, which extends beyond the project end date of 24 Dec 2026.
issues.fix: Adjust the wording to indicate that coverage will be monitored during the first week post‑go‑live (24‑30 Dec 2026) and reported as part of the hyper‑care period within the project timeframe.

issues.problem: The text states the first week of hyper-care is '24 Dec 2026 – 30 Dec 2026'. This contradicts the project end date of 24 Dec 2026 and the timeline in T3 which defines the Go-Live & Hypercare phase as 18 Dec - 24 Dec 2026. The 'first week post-go-live' should align with the defined hypercare period ending on the project end date.
issues.fix: Change the date range for the first week of hyper-care to '18 Dec 2026 – 24 Dec 2026' to align with the project end date and the timeline in T3.
